messages.text: Reading the COI form and the policy table first — the beside-form layout depends on which fields are already denormalised.
The form posts to /api/coi and the policy rows come from the policies table joined on programs. Two round trips today.
Found the duplicate: coverage_limits is fetched once for the form and again for the beside panel.
Collapsing both into one loader. That drops a query per keystroke on the limit fields.
RLS is the interesting part — the beside panel reads policies directly, so the org scope has to come from the same helper the form uses.
Using has_org_access(org_id) rather than re-deriving it. A second derivation is a second thing to get wrong.
Wrote the loader. Types generated clean.
The form renders beside the policy now, but the panel is a Client Component and pulls the whole policy payload.
Splitting it: the policy summary stays server-rendered, only the editable limits go client-side.
That took the initial payload from 180 KB to 34 KB.
Three states to cover: no policy yet, policy without limits, policy with limits. All three present.
The empty state was rendering an empty card with a border. Now it renders nothing and the form takes the full width.
Added the pgTap case for the RLS path — a user in another org gets zero rows, not an error.
Watched it go red first: dropping has_org_access from the policy select returns the other org's row.
Suite green. 14 new assertions.
Now the migration. coverage_limits needs a composite index on policy_id + coverage_id or the beside panel scans.
Index added in a new migration, not by editing the last one — that one is already applied on staging.
explain analyze: 340ms to 4ms on the worst program (14 coverages).
The proposal builder reads the same table. Checked it still uses the index — it does, same leading column.
Rebased on main. One conflict in the loader, resolved toward main's version of the org helper.
Lint clean. Build clean.
One thing I want to flag: the beside panel shows expired policies without saying they are expired.
Added an expired badge using the same amber the rest of the app uses for stale data.
The badge needed a date comparison in the loader, not the component, or it flashes wrong on hydration.
Screenshots taken at 390 and 1440 wide. The beside layout collapses to stacked under 900.
Wrote the user-guide section for the new panel.
Spec 24 3.8b mentions the beside form — updated it to match what I actually built.
Draft PR #1171 is up with both screenshots.
Review comment: use the shared PolicyBadge instead of a local one. Fair — doing that.
Swapped it. The shared badge already handles the expired case, so the date comparison moved into it.
That deleted 30 lines net.
Re-ran the suite after the swap. Still green.
Pushed. PR is ready for a second look.
All three states present. Running the full suite before I touch the migration.
